Back up and restore Postgres clusters

Base backups work with Postgres 9.6 and later. Streaming WAL through a replication slot works with
Postgres 14 and later. Base backups and WAL go into separate sets.

```sh
goback [global flags] postgres <command>
```

## postgres base

Take a base backup and commit it to the set named by --set

base connects with --dbname, or with PGHOST, PGUSER and the other PG* variables. The user needs
the REPLICATION attribute. On Postgres 15 and later, goback takes the backup over its own replication
connection. On older versions, or with --pg-basebackup, goback runs pg_basebackup to take it.

```sh
goback [global flags] postgres base [flags]
```

| Flag | Description | Environment | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--dbname value` | connection string for the backup | `GOBACK_POSTGRES_DBNAME` |  |
| `--pg-basebackup value` | pg_basebackup program to take the backup with; its major version must match the server's | `GOBACK_POSTGRES_BASEBACKUP` |  |

## postgres receive

Stream the cluster's WAL through a replication slot and commit it to the set named by --set until SIGTERM

receive connects with --dbname, or with PGHOST, PGUSER and the other PG* variables. The role
needs the REPLICATION attribute. pg_hba.conf needs a replication line for the role. It also needs a
line for a normal connection to the database in --dbname, which is postgres by default. The slot
holds the WAL that the receiver has not committed yet. Set max_slot_wal_keep_size to limit it. Run
receive --drop-slot when you retire the receiver.

```sh
goback [global flags] postgres receive [flags]
```

| Flag | Description | Environment | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--spool value` | directory that holds WAL until it is committed | `GOBACK_POSTGRES_SPOOL` |  |
| `--base-set value` | set that holds the cluster's base backups |  |  |
| `--dbname value` | connection string for the receiver | `GOBACK_POSTGRES_DBNAME` |  |
| `--slot value` | physical replication slot to use; goback_ followed by the set's name by default |  |  |
| `--commit-every value` | how often to commit new WAL; at least 10s |  | `1m0s` |
| `--commit-bytes value` | commit early once this much new WAL has arrived |  | `256MiB` |
| `--window value` | how far back point-in-time recovery reaches; WAL older than the oldest base backup in this window is retired |  | `336h0m0s` |
| `--allow-uncapped-slot` | stream even when max_slot_wal_keep_size does not limit the slot, so the slot can keep WAL until the database's disk is full |  |  |
| `--shutdown-grace value` | how long the last commit may take after SIGTERM |  | `30s` |
| `--drop-slot` | drop the replication slot and exit |  |  |

## postgres restore

Write a base backup into an empty data directory; with --wal-set, Postgres recovers from that WAL when it starts on the directory

With --wal-set, restore sets a restore_command that runs goback for each WAL file Postgres asks
for. It runs this binary with the global flags given here, or the command in --goback. The command
and its flags go into postgresql.auto.conf, or into recovery.conf before Postgres 12. Settings
given as environment variables must also be set in Postgres's environment. With --copy-wal, restore
copies the WAL into pg_wal instead. Postgres then needs neither goback nor the store.

```sh
goback [global flags] postgres restore [flags] <data directory>
```

| Flag | Description | Environment | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--base-set value` | set that holds the cluster's base backups; a number names the set by id and reads it from the store instead of the index |  |  |
| `--wal-set value` | set that holds the cluster's WAL, for recovering past the end of the base backup; a number names the set by id |  |  |
| `--at value` | moment to recover to, in RFC 3339 (2026-10-02T14:30:00Z); the end of the WAL set by default |  |  |
| `--goback value` | command that restore_command uses to run goback, including the global flags |  |  |
| `--copy-wal` | copy the WAL recovery reads into the data directory instead of fetching it through restore_command |  |  |

## postgres wal-get

Write one WAL file from a WAL commit to a path; restore_command runs this

```sh
goback [global flags] postgres wal-get [flags] <%f> <%p>
```

| Flag | Description | Environment | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--wal-set value` | set that holds the WAL commit |  |  |
| `--commit value` | ref of the WAL commit, in hex |  |  |
